claims: read_binding is total over arbitrary bytes, and bind over any schema-valid document and admitted model: only BindingError with a RULE_ORDER rule id is raised, never another exception.
The checks run in RULE_ORDER, and within a rule the first violation in sorted order is reported, so the message does not depend on the document's member order.

The semantic model is the binding's tables: datasets sorted by name, fields in document order, keys as given, one relationship per group of equal references with columns paired in table column order, relationship names unique. With no unique_keys member, each confirmed alethic uniqueness bound in one table that is not the primary key becomes a unique key.

Every role of a bound fact type is mapped from exactly the columns the binding lists, in the entity's identification order; a table.column string is resolved by lookup and never split; role names match by the D8 normalization and nothing else does.
Every fact type and constraint appears exactly once in the listing with the disposition the normative table states; the Rmap is not run; binding_sha256 is the digest of the file bytes.
Without --physical-binding every output is byte-identical to main before OB4 (the OB2 and OB3 corpora and the census baseline), and with it the ontology, sidecar and loss report are unchanged.
The SQL type map is closed and its lexer states the whole grammar it accepts; anything else leaves datatype absent and is never a refusal.

question: Does the OB4 implementation (gnd.export.physical_binding, its wiring in gnd.export.ossie, gnd.export.ossie_relational and gnd.commands.export, and the generalized gnd.rmap records) implement the approved OB4 spec (r1 with amendment r1.1, sections 6, 7, 12 and 13) and the normative 'Physical binding' subsection? Is there any binding file, of any bytes, or any schema-valid binding with any admitted model, for which gnd export ossie --physical-binding raises anything but a BindingError with a rule id from RULE_ORDER (or the model's own refusals), reports a later rule while an earlier one applies, writes a semantic model or mapping the pinned schemas or the documents' own cross references reject, maps a role to the wrong columns, omits a fact type or constraint from the listing, or changes any output of a run without the flag?
